open_points.subject: A09-1 rights-table invariant
open_points.question: Must A09-1 be shown for every service/operation pair in the rights table, or are the three named refusal examples intended to be sufficient evidence for the universal invariant?
options: Use a table-driven check covering every allowed operation and every operation outside each service's row.
Add separate Required tests that collectively cover the whole rights table.
Narrow A09-1 to only the examples currently tested.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the universal invariant and require a table-driven check for the complete rights table.

witness.initial: The release contains the A09 rights table, including operations not exercised by Required tests 1, 2 or 4.
events: A later agent implements the three named verification checks.
Another later agent treats A09-1 as requiring exhaustive validation of every row.
outcomes: Only Cabinet billing, Kernel context and PresuPro publishing are checked; an erroneous untested right can pass.
Every service/operation pair is checked, so an erroneous right fails verification.
witness.observer: The factory gate and a caller using an operation absent from the three examples.

open_points.subject: A10-1 three agent-authority checks
open_points.question: Which Required test must show each conjunct of A10-1: the Cabinet Kernel token, registration of the named session, and project membership, including the registration exception?
options: Add one table-driven test covering wrong token, unregistered session, outside-set project and registration's token-only exception.
Bind separate Required tests to each conjunct, including existing test 5 for registration.
Treat the outside-set and revocation examples as sufficient for all of A10-1.
open_points.default_guess: Add or bind tests that explicitly cover every conjunct and the registration exception.

witness.initial: A call uses Cabinet Kernel's valid token but names an unregistered session.
events: The call invokes a session operation other than registration.
outcomes: The call is refused as outside the set, explicitly showing the registration conjunct.
No linked test covers this history, so an implementation omitting the registration check can satisfy the named witnesses.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel and the invariant check.

open_points.subject: A12-1 and A12-2 access-version invariants
open_points.question: Must the Required tests show stale-version refusal and an increment of exactly one for every owner action and every accepted session change named by the rules, or only for replacement, grant, erasure and owner end?
options: Use a table-driven check for granting, revoking, changing or clearing active project, answering a request, ending, replacing a request and project erasure.
Add separate Required tests for the currently uncovered actions.
Accept the listed examples as representative of the universal invariants.
open_points.default_guess: Use a table-driven check covering every action named by A12 rules 1 and 3.

witness.initial: A registered session has version 4 and a granted active project.
events: The owner revokes that project while stating version 4.
The revocation changes both the granted set and active project.
outcomes: The version becomes 5 because one action moves it once.
The version becomes 6, or remains 4, while all currently linked A12 witnesses still pass.

open_points.subject: A08-1 authorized publishers and withdrawers
open_points.question: What Required test shows the complete accepted-caller implication in A08-1, including an accepted owner action and an accepted Kernel action on a granted project?
options: Bind test 4 and add an accepted Kernel-on-granted-project case to A08-1.
Use one table-driven check covering owner, authorized Kernel and every unauthorized service or session state.
Treat the two refusal examples as sufficient evidence for the implication about all accepted calls.
open_points.default_guess: Use a table-driven check covering both authorized principals and the refusal boundaries.

open_points.subject: A02-1 and A02-2 required values
open_points.question: Which Required tests show the invariants for the required object address and Customer kind, which are not named by the newly bound required-text check?
options: Extend the check to every required field, including object address and Customer kind.
Add separate Required tests for the missing required fields.
Treat the named text fields as representative of every required value.
open_points.default_guess: Extend the check to enumerate every required field.

open_points.subject: A03-2 non-editable project facts
open_points.question: What Required test shows that correcting a Project preserves all of that Project's non-editable facts, rather than showing A03-2 only for a Customer?
options: Add a Project correction test that asserts identity, status, marks, creation instant and request id remain unchanged.
Make the named verification check table-driven over both Project and Customer corrections and say so in the Required test.
Restrict A03-2 to Customer corrections.
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit Project coverage while retaining A03-2 for both record kinds.

witness.initial: A Project has an archived mark, creation instant and request id alongside editable facts.
events: The owner submits an accepted correction changing an editable fact.
The generated implementation rebuilds the Project record.
outcomes: One untested non-editable fact is lost or rewritten while the Customer-only A03-2 witness passes.
witness.observer: The owner reading the corrected project and later retrying its create.

open_points.subject: A04-3 revision movement for Customers
open_points.text:
A correction that changes a project moves its revision by exactly one and
   sets its last-changed instant to the current instant; one that changes
   nothing leaves both. Shows A04-3, A04-6.
open_points.question: What Required test shows A04-3 for accepted Customer changes, since the added exact-increment test covers only a Project?
options: Add a table-driven test for every Project and Customer action that keeps a revision.
Add at least one accepted Customer change that asserts revision plus one and matching last-changed movement.
Limit A04-3 to Project corrections.
open_points.default_guess: Use a table-driven check for every revision-moving action on both record kinds.

events: The owner accepts a correction that changes the Customer's contact data.
outcomes: The revision is 8 and the last-changed instant moves.
The revision jumps to 9 while all newly linked A04 tests still pass.
witness.observer: The owner and a later stale-change check.

open_points.subject: A11-2 re-registration state
open_points.text:
Registering the ended identity again answers a session with no project.
   Shows A11-2. [witness: verification:registry_a11_reregistered_ended_identity_empty]
open_points.question: Does “with no project” require both an empty granted set and no active project, as A11-2 states, and must the check also show that no pending request or prior access version survives?
options: Assert an empty granted set and no active project only, exactly matching A11-2.
Assert a wholly fresh session: empty granted set, no active project, no pending request and initial access version.
Assert only that the active project is absent.
open_points.default_guess: Assert a wholly fresh session, including the initial access version, because rule 4 says the registration makes a new session with an empty set.

witness.initial: An ended session previously had a nonempty granted set, an active project, a pending request and access version 6.
events: Cabinet Kernel registers the ended identity again.
Kernel reads the new session's access.
outcomes: The new session has an empty set, no active project, no pending request and version 1.
It has no active project but retains a stale grant, request or version; both can be described informally as a session with “no project.”
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel and the owner listing sessions.

open_points.subject: A22 Required test 4 historical type set
open_points.text:
In the first release publishing `estimate` is accepted and its pointer
   names PresuPro, and publishing each v1 type (L08) is refused as an unknown
   type. Shows A22-1.
open_points.question: What exact set does “each v1 type (L08)” mean, since the supplied texts do not list L08's members?
options: List every historical v1 type explicitly in A22 Required test 4.
Replace the historical reference with a closed set supplied through an accepted model or policy value.
Test one named undeclared type and remove the claim that every v1 type is exercised.
open_points.default_guess: List the historical v1 type names explicitly so the test generator has a closed domain.

events: One generator guesses the old v1 vocabulary from memory.
Another generator knows a different historical L08 list.
Both generate the A22 verification check.
outcomes: Only the first guessed set of old types is refused by the check.
A different set is exercised, leaving some historical type untested.
witness.observer: The factory check and a caller publishing an omitted historical type.

open_points.subject: Unbound Required tests in A09, A10, A12, A07, A08, A15, A16, A17, A18, A19, A01, A03 and A05
open_points.text: each Required tests item has a witness check that asserts the invariants it names
open_points.question: Which concrete witness check will bind each Required tests item that still has no `[witness: ...]` binding after the unit-level note witnesses were removed?
options: Bind each item to an existing verification check during assembly.
Create a dedicated verification check where no existing check asserts the item's result.
Combine several items in one check only when that check explicitly asserts every listed result.
open_points.default_guess: During State 8 assembly, reuse an existing check only when its assertions match the full item; otherwise create a dedicated check.
consequences: Reusing a check reduces duplication but can leave an item nominally bound to evidence that does not assert its result.
Dedicated checks give direct evidence but increase the verification suite.
Leaving an item unbound violates the accepted handoff requirement and prevents a complete assembly.
open_points.requirement: each Required tests item has a witness check that asserts the invariants it names
